newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan receives cordial invitation from Helms.
newsitem.headline: Annan receives cordial invitation from Helms.

text.p: Senator Jesse Helms, chairman of the powerful U.S. Senate foreign relations committee, on Thursday invited Secretary-General-elect Kofi Annan of Ghana to meet the committee and begin a dialogue on U.N. reform.

Helms, a Republican from North Carolina, has been a strong critic of the United Nations and current secretary-general Boutros Boutros-Ghali, who leaves office at the end of the month after the United States vetoed his re-election.

Helms told Annan in a letter: "It would be an honour and pleasure to host a committee coffee for your visit, and formally introduce you to the U.S. Senators who play a key role in determining U.S. policy on the U.N.
"I feel such a meeting could very well begin a constructive dialogue."

Congratulating Annan on his election, Helms said he faced the challenge of "demonstrating that the United Nations is not impervious to reform; that it can be downsized, brought under control, and harnessed to contribute to the security needs of the 21st century."
"If you choose to be an agent of real and deep-seated change, you will find many supporters -- even allies -- here in the U.S. Congress," Helms said.
"It is my hope that we can work together to accomplish these goals and set the U.N. on a path of true reform."

Annan told a questioner at a U.N. news conference Wednesday he expected to work with the U.S. administration, and through it with Congress, "to get the United States to pay the money due the organisation."
He was referring to the approximately $1.3 billion which the United States owes the cash-strapped United Nations in unpaid dues and for its share of peacekeeping costs.
Annan said it was "not really in the interest of the United States not to pay its contribution to the United Nations. It offends friends and foes alike," he added.
"The United States needs the United Nations and the United Nations needs the United States. We cannot operate effectively and efficiently without a sound financial basis," he said.
"I am confident that the administration will do all that it can. We on our side also have to do what is expected of us. By this I mean ongoing in reforms," Annan said.
